divergences: N^-1 inverse-length scale: Impl1 used the spec-stated 8857; Impl2 rejected it as a numeric error and used 12277 (1024^-1 mod 12289), since 8857*1024 ≡ 286 ≠ 1 — the spec carries a self-inconsistent N_inv value.

Conflict-free bank mapping b(i)=(i+(i>>3))%8: Impl1 declared it conflict-free over 8-index blocks; Impl2 proved it puts a radix-2 operand pair (i, i+2^6) in the SAME bank at stage 6 — the spec left the actual per-stage permutation unspecified so the two reached opposite conclusions about the headline property.
Transform flavor: both leaned negacyclic, but the spec explicitly marks cyclic-vs-negacyclic as 'unstated in source' — convergence was a shared guess, not a specified fact.

Conflict-free read/write addressing semantics ('no bit-reversal'): both reproduced output VALUES recursively (natural order by construction) rather than the hardware's actual crossbar permutation, because the spec never gives the stage permutations σ_s.

missing_fields.item: Correct inverse-length constant N^-1 mod q (spec states 8857, which is wrong; correct value is 12277)
Transform flavor explicitly stated (negacyclic vs cyclic) rather than 'unstated/implied'
The paper's actual conflict-free bank-index b(i) and offset o(i) functions plus per-stage read/write permutations σ_s (the headline Sec. III result)
Twiddle-factor ROM contents, the chosen primitive root/generator binding, and ROM addressing/indexing scheme
Bank addressing map from coefficient index to BRAM bank under interleaving
Reported pipeline cycle counts (mult/add-sub/Barrett/reg) — spec marks 3/1/4/1 as reproduction defaults pending the paper
Radix-2/4 config-selector schedule / FSM state table and loop bounds governing radix switching

parameter_fidelity.impl_value: 8 (declared, but modeled recursively, not as 8 parallel lanes)
radix-2 and radix-4 both implemented and proven equal

property_checks.property: Conflict-free memory mapping (arbitrary radix/#BU, no bank conflict)
property_checks.evidence: Reconstructed map b(i)=(i+(i>>3))%8 provably collides at stage s=6 (Impl2); the paper's real mapping was never transcribed.
Impls produce natural-order values recursively by construction, not via the hardware's no-bit-reversal addressing.

property_checks.property: Radix-4 uses 33% fewer mults / 20% fewer add/sub than radix-2
property_checks.evidence: Only the radix-4 BU equation was checked equal to DFT-4; the quantified op-count savings were not formally verified.

property_checks.property: ~50% butterfly hardware saved via symmetric operators
property_checks.evidence: Purely a hardware-area claim; functional impls model no hardware, so it cannot be exhibited.

property_checks.property: NTT followed by INTT (with N^-1) is identity
property_checks.evidence: Both verify round-trip identity (Impl2 with the corrected N^-1=12277; Impl1 only round-trips if 8857 is consistent — its scale value is suspect).

structural_findings: Hardware is an iterative/in-place datapath with an interleaved 8-bank BRAM + crossbar; both impls are recursive Cooley-Tukey with no banks, no crossbar, and no parallel lanes — the central conflict-free memory architecture is absent.
The paper's headline contribution (conflict-free mapping for arbitrary radix and #BU) is not reproduced; the bank map used is a spec-flagged guess that one impl proves conflicting.
Radix switching is modeled by recursively swapping radix-2/radix-4 routines rather than via the schedule/FSM config selector that reconfigures 8 lanes into 4 fused radix-4 BUs.
Pipeline latency, PCIe/DMA framing, FIFO handshake and twiddle broadcast are documented only as comments — none of the timing/interface structure is exercised.

summary: Reproducibility is capped by two spec gaps that made the impls diverge: a self-inconsistent N^-1 constant (8857 is wrong; correct is 12277) and the un-transcribed conflict-free bank/permutation functions, which the two impls disagree about (conflict-free vs provably conflicting at stage 6). Fidelity is moderate: the functional NTT uses the right named parameters (q=12289, N=1024, 14-bit, Barrett mu=21843/k=28, negacyclic, round-trip identity), but the paper's actual contributions — the conflict-free interleaved-BRAM/crossbar architecture, the no-bit-reversal addressing, and the quantified radix-4 op-count/hardware savings — are not reproduced, leaving only a generic correct NTT rather than the specific CFNTT datapath.
guessed: Transform flavor (source: 'unstated') -> negacyclic NTT (mod x^N+1) via explicit psi^i pre-twist / psi^-i post-twist, since the spec's metadata leans negacyclic for PQC/HE
Primitive roots -> psi = 11^6 = 1945 (order 2048), omega = psi^2 = 10302 (order 1024), j = psi^512 (order 4); taken from spec's reproduction-chosen generator g=11
Negacyclic method -> separate pre/post twist tables (not merged-into-butterfly twiddles), matching the spec's 'low/high half' ROM note
Datapath structure -> recursive radix-2 and radix-4 DIT producing natural order (the hardware is iterative/in-place; modeled recursively so output equals the direct DFT with no bit-reversal)
Barrett correction bound -> exactly 2 conditional subtractions suffice; proven by z3 over the actual operand-product domain x <= (q-1)^2
Conflict-free property tested -> 'every block of 8 consecutive indices maps to 8 distinct banks' (the spec's full per-stage permutation sigma_s is flagged reproduction-guessed and not transcribed)
INTT -> ntt with omega^-1 then scale by N^-1=8857; NTT∘INTT = identity
Pipeline latencies (mult 3 / add-sub 1 / Barrett 4 / reg 1 = 9) -> timing only, not modeled in functional output
Op-count claims (33% fewer mults, 20% fewer add/sub, ~50% HW) -> not formally verified; only the radix-4 BU equation (3 twiddle mults + j-rotator) is checked equal to the DFT-4
Inverse-length scale N^-1: spec states N_inv_value=8857, but 1024^-1 mod 12289 = 12277 (8857*1024 ≡ 286, not 1). Used the mathematically correct 12277; the spec's 8857 is a numeric error.
Transform flavor -> negacyclic (psi a 2N=2048-th root, omega=psi^2), following the spec's stated lean; cyclic fallback rejected.
Primitive roots from g=11: psi=11^6 mod q=1945 (order 2048, psi^1024≡-1), omega=psi^2=10302, j=psi^512=omega^256 (order-4 rotator) — spec-provided, verified at runtime.

Output ordering -> recursive Cooley-Tukey producing natural order by construction; the hardware's exact crossbar permutation sigma_s / 'no-bit-reversal' addressing is NOT bit-true reproduced (only the values are).
Radix-4 butterfly = DFT4 applied to (x0, w*x1, w^2*x2, w^3*x3) with constant 4th root j; matched to spec equations exactly and to the same constant j across all recursion levels.
Barrett: t=(x*mu)>>28, r=x-t*q, up to 2 conditional subtractions; 2 corrections proven sufficient for all 28-bit inputs via z3.

Conflict-free bank map b(i)=(i+(i>>3))%8, o(i)=i>>3 (spec-provided) — my analysis shows it does NOT keep radix-2 operand pairs (i, i+2^s) in distinct banks at stage s=6 (2^6=64): a genuine conflict. Reported, not gated, since the spec itself flags this map as a guess.
Pipeline latencies (mult 3 / add-sub 1 / Barrett 4 / reg 1) and PCIe/DMA/FIFO/FSM control are functionally irrelevant to the transform value; modeled only as comments, not cycle-accurately.
